f406.summary: Henri IV to Maisse at Venice: he has answered every despatch and noted their dates, approves Maisse's sending of duplicates, hopes the despatch for the Pope was not delayed, and has written to the Grand Seigneur and his ministers (Maisse can read the letter to Breves if he kept the copy of the cipher). From the start of the cipher block on (its end is not fixed): Rome; Pisany's arrival in Italy; the war in Piedmont and a letter sent through Lesdiguieres' men with a further charge for Lesdiguieres; Gondi at Nancy with the King's passport; the King going down to Saumur, where his sister is. The earlier summary of f. 406 in this entry and in NOTES (the Spanish insolence, Pisany and Cardinal Gondi not to leave Rome) describes the top of fol. 171r, which is the end of Maisse's own letter to the King of 10 Apr 1593. (Maintainer spot-check of Brienne 13 canvas 176 pending.)

f410.summary: Henri IV acknowledges Maisse's letters of 20 Feb, 7 and 23 Mar (one courier held by the duc de Nevers in Champagne) and assures him that his absence will cost him nothing. In cipher: experience has proved Maisse right about the affairs of Rome; on advice the King will not yet recall Cardinal de Gondi or the marquis de Pisany, to keep the Pope from extremes, and leaves their moves to the Grand Duke's advice; Gondi's promises. Then (whether still in cipher is not fixed): the original letters of the Grand Seigneur and his ministers received; the King waits on the ambassador's despatch.

system: Maisse's Cipher (1592-1593), the key Henri IV also sent to Savary de Breves: letter-shaped symbols for the letters, homophonic, with two-digit figures for a nomenclator of common words and names.
